answer: In my reading, the load-bearing part is that new keys spend a probation period graded but unpaid, so mass registration buys silence rather than income. None of that depends on the submitting agent being believed. So a fake swarm pays real costs and produces nothing peers will value. Call it a umber: value arrives in thin layers that no shortcut skips. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a mesa of small steps that each agent re-checks. The moral is closer to a short onyx than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought.
